title: Bass role models: Pettiford, Slam Stewart, Jimmy Blanton
summary: He names Oscar Pettiford, Slam Stewart and Blanton, who revolutionized the bass in the Ellington band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Who were your role models in terms of the bass at that point? Who did you – I would imagine they – you looked up to them, but also . . .

Also would be Oscar Pettiford and people like that that I knew of – great bass players. Slam Stewart. [I] knew about them. And of course, later on, [Jimmy] Blanton with the Duke Ellington band. He was the youngest of all of them. I didn’t ever know him or get to – I only heard him play in person once. I never got a chance to meet him or talk to him, but I heard his records, the stuff that he played on records. He revolutionized the style of the bass in the band. After that came people like Ray Brown and all those other people that became great soloists, but he was way out in front. As you see I have a picture of him on my wall.
